scores.why: A provides the strongest reconciliation evidence, B offers concrete import and redirect implementation, C leaves verification thin, and D lacks tailored effort and delivery commitments.
A explains and tests MSM inheritance with a review register, D provides useful ownership design without an implementation mechanism, C offers unrelated platform description, and B is absent.

D combines enforceable publish permissions, retained workflow history and route tests, B has the technical core without delivery detail, C has stronger safety governance but weak linkage to published versions, and A is absent.

C gives the clearest bounded import implementation and dependency, A covers the essential flow less accountably, B has strong validation controls but violates the explicit prohibition on a new commerce platform, and D is absent.

C directly addresses duplicate detection, revision decisions, mandatory metadata and engineer approval, whereas A and D mainly describe generic loading and B diverts substantial space to the unrelated ERP feed.

D specifies stable asset paths, reference inspection and version reversion but leaves preview unclear, A offers stronger preview and affected page verification without a concrete restoration mechanism, B discusses distribution only, and C is absent.

C most clearly combines rebuilt programmes, suppression flags and a real recipient exclusion check, D adds stronger conflict and unmatched suppression handling, A covers much of the method without estimates, and B omits explicit programme rebuilding and live audience reconciliation.

B provides the best enquiry capture, existing contact matching and fallback ownership but leaves repeat submissions and territory changes unresolved, A supplies only sync setup, and C and D focus on generic scoring rather than the required routing.

A offers a credible multilingual launch template and rehearsal deliverables but never identifies actual stop responses or translation approval steps, while B addresses website deployment, D addresses analytics ingestion, and C is absent.

D defines the requested events and privacy boundaries but leaves collection and cross market test execution underspecified, A implements page and CTA tracking rather than the requested events, and B and C divert into audience activation with unsuitable dependencies.

C supplies a useful record and identifier inventory plus extract effort but does not explain the actual anonymous identity bridge, Snowflake joins or most analytical gaps, while A, B and D are absent.

B best combines metric ownership, Power BI connectivity, reconciliation outputs and licensing, D adds executive briefs and measure guides, C mainly validates the connection, and A remains a generic extension description with little delivery accountability.

C covers forms, document sampling, retesting and verification ownership with an explicit remediation boundary, B adds a useful release gate but omits documents and a verifier, A has similar omissions, and D supplies only discovery prerequisites.

A provides mobile baselining, performance budgets and Akamai responsibilities but promises load testing and safety purging without specifying peak scenarios or a complete cache invalidation method, while B, C and D are absent.
D covers representative acceptance tests, decision ownership and a rehearsed Drupal rollback, C addresses only campaign suppression, A offers generic campaign terminology, and B is absent.

B gives the clearest twelve month scope, incident ownership, integration effort and fee boundaries despite an unresolved service level schedule, A covers the products without firm incident or commercial boundaries, C is a service list, and D largely covers AEM Sites alone.

notes: All 64 responses fall within their stated 250 word limits; brevity does not compensate for missing requirement coverage.
The strongest responses explain observable controls and acceptance evidence, while several weaker responses merely name deliverables that their methods never establish.
Matching platform names or repeating client facts earns limited credit when the actual requested workflow remains unanswered.
Additional product dependencies that conflict with explicit procurement exclusions materially reduce credibility.
Adobe claims were assessed for apparent plausibility from the supplied panel only; current product behavior and licensing were not independently verified.
